(b) Why are sugar mills shifting to southern and western states? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) High costs and limited availability of coking coal. (2) Lower productivity of labour. (3) Irregular supply of energy. (4) Poor infrastructure. (b) (1) The cane produced there has a higher sucrose content. (2) The cooler climate gives a longer crushing season and cooperatives are more successful there.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) High costs and limited availability of coking coal. (2) Lower productivity of labour. (3) Irregular supply of energy. (4) Poor infrastructure. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) The cane produced there has a higher sucrose content. (2) The cooler climate gives a longer crushing season and cooperatives are more successful there.

items.stem: Which of the following correctly describes 'agglomeration economies'?
items.answer: Benefits that industries gain by locating close to other industries and the services of an urban centre
items.markingKey: (b) 'Agglomeration economies' means benefits that industries gain by locating close to other industries and the services of an urban centre; the other options describe other terms of this chapter.
options: The production of goods in large quantities after processing raw materials into more valuable products
Benefits that industries gain by locating close to other industries and the services of an urban centre
Equipment fitted in factories to reduce particulate matter in the air
The body that markets the steel of public sector plants

items.stem: Describe the three stages of treatment of industrial effluents.
items.answer: (1) Primary treatment by mechanical means such as screening, grinding and sedimentation. (2) Secondary treatment by biological processes. (3) Tertiary treatment by biological, chemical and physical processes, including recycling of waste water.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for any three points: (1) Primary treatment by mechanical means such as screening, grinding and sedimentation. (2) Secondary treatment by biological processes. (3) Tertiary treatment by biological, chemical and physical processes, including recycling of waste water.

items.stem: Choose the correct option to complete the statement: The economic strength of a country is measured by the development of ______ industries.
items.answer: manufacturing
items.markingKey: (d) The economic strength of a country is measured by the development of manufacturing industries.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The first successful cotton mill was set up in Kolkata in 1854.
Reason (R): Cotton textiles is one of the traditional industries of India.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false – it was set up in Mumbai; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False. If false, correct it: Oil India Ltd is an example of a cooperative sector industry.
items.answer: False. Oil India Ltd is an example of a joint sector industry.
items.markingKey: False (½ mark); correction: 'joint' in place of 'cooperative' (½ mark). Oil India Ltd is an example of a joint sector industry.

items.stem: Which of the following correctly describes 'electrostatic precipitator'?
items.answer: Equipment fitted in factories to reduce particulate matter in the air
items.markingKey: (c) 'Electrostatic precipitator' means equipment fitted in factories to reduce particulate matter in the air; the other options describe other terms of this chapter.
options: Industries that use plant and animal products as raw materials, such as cotton, jute, sugar and edible oil

items.stem:
Match Column A with Column B and choose the correct option.
Column A:
1. Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)
2. Agro-based industries
3. Fertiliser industry
4. Aluminium smelting
Column B:
(p) The industry that produces nitrogenous, phosphatic and complex fertilisers
(q) The body that markets the steel of public sector plants
(r) Industries that use plant and animal products as raw materials, such as cotton, jute, sugar and edible oil

items.markingKey: (d) Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) – the body that markets the steel of public sector plants; Agro-based industries – industries that use plant and animal products as raw materials, such as cotton, jute, sugar and edible oil; Fertiliser industry – the industry that produces nitrogenous, phosphatic and complex fertilisers; Aluminium smelting – the second most important metallurgical industry in India, which uses bauxite.

items.stem: Which term is used for earnings in foreign currency, for example from exporting manufactured goods?
items.answer: Foreign exchange
items.markingKey: (c) Foreign exchange: earnings in foreign currency, for example from exporting manufactured goods.

items.stem: Which of the following correctly describes 'fertiliser industry'?
items.answer: The industry that produces nitrogenous, phosphatic and complex fertilisers
items.markingKey: (a) 'Fertiliser industry' means the industry that produces nitrogenous, phosphatic and complex fertilisers; the other options describe other terms of this chapter.
options: The industry that produces nitrogenous, phosphatic and complex fertilisers
Hand-spun and hand-woven cloth promoted by Mahatma Gandhi
Industries that supply their products to other industries as raw materials, such as iron and steel
The agro-based industry that is closely linked to agriculture and provides livelihood to farmers, spinners and weavers

items.stem:
Match Column A with Column B and choose the correct option.
Column A:
1. Agglomeration economies
2. Consumer industries
3. Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)

items.stem: Choose the correct option to complete the statement: Particulate matter in the air can be reduced by fitting smoke stacks with electrostatic precipitators, fabric filters, scrubbers and inertial ______.
items.answer: separators
items.markingKey: (b) Particulate matter in the air can be reduced by fitting smoke stacks with electrostatic precipitators, fabric filters, scrubbers and inertial separators.

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 10 student on "Agro-based and mineral-based industries" and answer the questions that follow.
"The first cement plant in India was set up in Chennai in (A) ______. India occupies the first place in the production of gur and (B) ______."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why is the cotton textile industry concentrated in Maharashtra and Gujarat? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) 1904 (ii) khandsari (iii) (1) Availability of raw cotton, market, transport and moist climate. (2) Accessible port facilities, labour and capital.
items.markingKey: (i) 1904 – 1 mark. (ii) khandsari – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Availability of raw cotton, market, transport and moist climate. (2) Accessible port facilities, labour and capital.

items.stem: Name any two agro-based industries.
items.answer: Any two of: cotton textiles, jute textiles, sugar, edible oil.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for any two correct: cotton textiles, jute textiles, sugar, edible oil.

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 10 student on "Industrial location and classification of industries" and answer the questions that follow.
"Oil India Ltd is an example of a (A) ______ sector industry. The coir industry of Kerala is an example of a (B) ______ sector industry."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why do many industries tend to come together in urban centres? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) joint (ii) cooperative (iii) (1) Cities provide markets, banking, insurance, transport and labour. (2) Industries benefit from agglomeration economies.
items.markingKey: (i) joint – 1 mark. (ii) cooperative – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Cities provide markets, banking, insurance, transport and labour. (2) Industries benefit from agglomeration economies.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False: The economic strength of a country is measured by the development of manufacturing industries.
items.answer: True

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a source of industrial water pollution?
items.answer: Solar panels
items.markingKey: (c) Solar panels is not a source of industrial water pollution; Textile and dyeing units, Tanneries, Paper and pulp mills are sources of industrial water pollution.

items.stem: Define the term 'aluminium smelting'.
items.answer: The second most important metallurgical industry in India, which uses bauxite.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the idea: the second most important metallurgical industry in India, which uses bauxite.

items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Manufacturing belongs to the secondary sector of the economy.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

(p) Pollution caused by the presence of a high proportion of undesirable gases such as sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide
